div.l: And haue þanke and yit a cote and a hode
In youth he had lerned a good myster
He was a gode wright a carpenter
This reue sat vpon a wel good stotte
That was pomely grey and hight scotte
A longe surcote of ypres vppon he hadde
And bi his side he bare a lusti blade
Of northfolk was þis reve of which I tell
Beside a town̄ þat hight baldeswell
Tukked he was as a frere a bought
And euermore he rode hynmost of our route
A sompnour was with vs in that place
That had a faire rede cherubyns face
For sawcefleme he was with yen narowe
And hote he was and lecherous as a sparowe
With scalled browes blak and pilled berde
Of his visage childeren wer a ferde
There nas quik siluer lytarge nor brymstone
Boras ceruse ne oile of tarter none
Nor oynement þat wold clense and bite
That him might help of his whelkes wight
Nor of þe clobbes sitting in his chekes
Wel loued he garleke oynons and lekes
And for to drink strang win as blode
Than wold he slepe and crie as he wer wode
And whan he had wel dronken þe wyne
Than nold he speke no worde but latyne
A fewe termes had he ij . or iij .
That he had lerned oute of som̄ decre
No wondre is he herd it al þe day
And eke ye know wel þat a Iay
Can clepe wat aswel as þe pope
But who couth him in oþer þingꝭes grope
Than hadde he spent al his philosophi
A questio que iuris wold he crie
He was a gentel harlot and a kinde
A better felow shuld no man finde
He wold suffre for a quarte of wyn̄
A goode felawe to haue his concubine
A twel mounth and excuse him atte full
Ful priveli a fyn eke couth he pull
And if he fande any goode felawe
He wold teche him to haue none awe
